newsitem.title: UK: Unionamerica buys Lloyd's of London investor Jago.
newsitem.headline: Unionamerica buys Lloyd's of London investor Jago.

text.p: Unionamerica said on Monday it had acquired a 51 percent stake in Jago Dedicated Ltd, the sole shareholder in Jago Capital Ltd, a dedicated Lloyds of London corporate capital vehicle.
Jago Capital provides capacity for non-marine insurance syndicate 205, Unionamerica Holdings, a London market insurer and reinsurer, said in a statement.

"Unionamerica sees this move as providing synergy for the company...(it) will complement and strengthen our short-tail and non-U.S. business by giving us access...to different markets and clients," Philip Marcell, Unionamerica chairman, said.
"This is a good deal for Unionamerica and provides long term capital commitment for the Jago group," he added.
U.S. broker Aon Corp has a minority stake through a subsidiary in Jago Dedicated. Most of the rest of the shares are held by Jago management and staff.
Marcell said the deal also fitted in with Unionamerica's strategy of developing a community of interest with its major producing brokers.
Syndicate 205 has made profits in every year since it began in 1975 and has capacity -- the maximum amount of premium income it can underwrite -- of approximately 120 million stg, the statement said.
Jago Capital currently contributes about four percent of capacity.

Unionamerica said it and other companies are also in discussions with JMA Holdings, the holding company of Jago Managing Agency Limited, "about a possible acquisition of a minority shareholding in the holding company."
Many insurance companies have recently bought into Lloyd's managing agencies, the companies which run the market's insurance syndicates.
This trend follows Lloyd's implementation of its reconstruction plan last year and also reflects the decline in support from the market's traditional individual backers known as Names.
